newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark expects Nats to stay until deal struck.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark expects Nats to stay until deal struck.

text.p: New Zealand First would probably support the continuation of the conservative National caretaker government if a vote of no confidence was held while coalition talks were still under way, Labour leader Helen Clark said on Friday.
However, if National tried to implement its programme, breaking the caretaker convention, she expected NZ First would see that as provocative and might vote against it.
National's allies -- free market Act New Zealand and the one MP United Party -- have urged National to do that.
"What I would expect to happen is, if coalition talks are still alive, NZ First's position will be to maintain the status quo," Clark told NZPA.
Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating with both National and Labour over the shape of the next government.
NZ First could keep National in office either by voting for it or by abstaining on a motion of no confidence.
Clark said she had not discussed with NZ First what stance it would take.

On Thursday, in answer to journalists' questions she said she and National Prime Minister Jim Bolger would be seeking votes of confidence if a coalition had not been formed by the time Parliament was due to resume on December 13.
She later downplayed the comment, saying it was traditional for the opposition to move a vote of no confidence in the government after Parliament resumes.
"The mere calling of parliament does put everyone on notice that a decision of some sort has to be taken," she added today.
Clark said coalition talks were making good progress and were "starting to speed up a bit".
She was hopeful a coalition government could be formed before parliament resumed, although there were still policy and process issues to be resolved.
"I think it's getting close to the point at which NZ First could make a decision."
Clark said despite speculation over what might happen if a vote of no confidence in National was held, she did not expect such a vote would be taken.
If a coalition government had not been formed before parliament resumed, National would try to adjourn parliament before a no-confidence vote could be taken.
NZ First would probably support that, she said.
NZ First leader Winston Peters on Thursday disagreed with Clark that a motion of no confidence would be needed if a government had not been formed when Parliament resumed.
"The calling of parliament does not necessitate a confidence motion," he said.
